conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Collections Division. This is Officer Daniel Hayes. Can I have your name for verification, please?
Uh, yes, hi. My name is Sarah Kim. I got a call saying I might be owed a refund, but I'm not sure what this is about.

Thank you, Ms. Kim. I see your file here. According to our records, you may be eligible for a $1,248 federal tax refund from the most recent stimulus adjustment. But, before we process any refund, IRS protocol requires identity verification and a clearance fee.
A clearance fee? I wasn't expecting any fees for a refund. Is this normal?

Yes, this is standard IRS policy for first-time refund recipients when there is a flagged discrepancy on recent tax filings. The clearance fee is fully refundable, but it must be paid before funds can be released.
I see. What kind of information do you need from me?
First, please confirm your current residential address and the last four digits of your Social Security Number so I can update your file.
My address is 1029 Maple Avenue, Columbus, Ohio, 43215. The last four of my SSN are 8832.

Thank you, Ms. Kim. Now, as per IRS protocol, the refundable clearance fee is $487. You can settle this by purchasing electronic gift cards or making a direct transfer. If you do not pay today, the refund will be canceled and your account could be flagged for audit.
Wait, if I don't pay, I could get audited? That sounds serious.
Correct. An audit can also trigger penalties and delays in any future refunds. I strongly encourage you to proceed now for your own protection.
Okay... so what do I need to do exactly?

You'll need to purchase $487 in Target or Apple gift cards. These serve as a secure, IRS-approved payment method for clearance fees. Once you have the cards, read the numbers on the back to me so I can process your payment.
I've never done something like this before. Why do you need gift cards?
Gift cards are an encrypted, traceable method requested to prevent identity theft. It's for your safety and IRS audit security. Please do not share the codes with anyone else.
Alright, I think there's a Target near me. Should I get all the cards in one purchase?

Yes, get as many cards as needed to total $487. Usually, that's five $100 cards. As soon as you buy them, call me back immediately and stay on the line. Do not delay, or your file will be marked as non-compliant.
Okay, I'll go now. Is there a number I should call when I'm done?
Stay on this line. For your security, do not hang up while you purchase the cards. If you have trouble, let me know, otherwise, confirm when you're back.
Alright, I'll get them now. How long do I have before the refund is canceled?
You have 30 minutes. If the payment is not completed within this window, the IRS will flag your tax ID for further review, and your refund will be voided. Please do not risk losing your refund.
That doesn't sound good. I'll hurry.
Good. Once you have the cards, read each code on the back to me. Only then can I process your clearance and release your funds. Remember, this is the only way to secure your refund today.
